request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes (1/1). The test signs in as "uma" and "vic" in separate browsers on the same sheet and checks that each shows its own name and the sheet id. The TypeScript type check also passes.

**Server**
- A new database table stores sheets by id (`db/migration/V1__sheet.sql`).
- A new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}`, returns the sheet with that id. If the id has never been used, it creates an empty one. It's wired in `officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}.PUT.yml`, and the code is in `net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet`.

**Front end**
- I added a session bar under the nav, with two parts in `features/session/`:
  - **Sign in** (`signin.slot.tsx`): type a name and submit; after that the bar shows "Signed in as <name>". There's no password.
  - **Sheet picker** (`sheet.slot.tsx`): appears once you're signed in. Type an id and load it to call the endpoint; the active sheet id then shows. If the server refuses, an error message appears, and it clears when you edit the id.
- The signed-in name and the active sheet id are kept in the URL (`user` and `sheet`), following the app's convention for state that outlives a click. A side effect is that anyone with a link containing `user=` is signed in as that name, which fits having no password.
- `session.ts` gives later features one place to read the current user and sheet. When a sheet is loaded, the app re-fetches any saved data filed under that sheet id, so later per-sheet features will show fresh data when the sheet is loaded again.
